decoherence in Planck scale physics is not a well-defined notion and that it is not the right approach to the study of the microscopic structure of spacetime.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current understanding of decoherence in Planckian quantum gravity is still far from satisfactory.
decoherence in the context of quantum gravity is not well understood and needs more careful scrutiny.
decoherence in the quantum gravity context has been overhyped and is not as useful as it is often claimed to be.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
decoherence in the Planck energy regime is a process which is neither fundamental nor generic.
decoherence in the quantum gravity scale does not lead to the violation of the CPT symmetry and the thermalization of the spacetime foam.
decoherence is not a fundamental process in quantum gravity and that it does not lead to the emergence of spacetime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quantum decoherence at the Planck scale cannot be understood as the decoherence of a system in an environment.

the decoherence in quantum theory is a process which is not necessarily a physical one, and that decoherence in the Planck regime does not necessarily imply a classical spacetime, and hence a classical theory of gravity.
decoherence in Planck scale quantum gravity has to be understood as a stochastic process in a nonlocal theory, and that this process has no direct relation to decoherence in the open systems context.
